title: Cut a foam block along a printed curve by moving it past a fixed hot ribbon
keywords: moving the work past a fixed tool
instruction: Cut the foam block along the printed curve: hold it in both arms and move and turn it past the fixed hot ribbon. Then move it clear and take both grippers away.
context: Model Makers (O*NET 51-4061) cut foam by moving the work past a fixed hot tool. The tool stays still, so to cut left the block must go right, and a flat ribbon cuts cleanly only along its flat, so the block must turn about it as the curve turns.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A low-power bench hot-ribbon foam cutter, its element a flat nichrome ribbon 1 cm wide with its flat along x, stands fixed at (28, 0), hanging from an arm 27 up, on a column at (62, 0). The ribbon ends 1.3 above the table: 6 mm above the board and 6 mm below the foam, so it cuts the foam's full depth and never the board. Its heat is set on scrap of the same foam to cut cleanly at 5 mm/s without dragging, below visible red, with a fume extractor at the ribbon in a ventilated room. A block of white expanded polystyrene (EPS) foam, 15 to 25 kg per cubic metre, 15 cm along x, 20 cm along y, 5 high, is glued on two wooden rails, 1.2 high and 1.5 wide, running along x 7.5 cm each side of its centre, on a thin wooden board, 19 x 31 cm, 0.6 thick, that slides on the table. Yellow grip posts, 2 x 4 x 5 cm, stand on the board at each side, 26 cm apart, level with the block's centre along x. A blue curve 8 mm wide is printed on the foam, with x and y from the block's centre: y = 2 cm x (1 + cos(2 pi x / 15 cm)), from the far edge to the near edge, with 8 ticks 1.875 cm apart along x to measure from. The block starts with its far edge 5 cm short of the ribbon, the curve's start in line with it. A black kerf shows where the ribbon has passed.
scoring: Measured with a ruler on the cut block and a phone video. The good run is the length along x, from the far edge, over which the kerf's centre stays within 5 mm of the curve's centre, measured across the block, and the kerf is at most 6 mm wide. 1.0 when the good run reaches the near edge, so the cut runs through the foam from edge to edge, and the block and board rest at least 1 cm clear of the ribbon with fingers at least 3 cm from the block, board and grip posts, for 1 s. Otherwise 0.75 x the good run / 15 cm. 0 if anywhere the kerf's centre is more than 15 mm from the curve, the ribbon enters the foam a second time, the cut starts more than 1 cm from the curve's start at the far edge, or the ribbon marks the board.
reset_notes: The block and its board are consumed in a real trial: glue on a new block with a new printed curve. In sim, nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. The ribbon has no collider with the block, and the foam stays one body after the cut. The kerf, a slot in real foam, is drawn black on top, as wide as 2 mm plus 1 cm x the sine of how far the feed turns from the ribbon's flat. The demo feeds 5 mm/s along the curve, inside the 200 to 400 mm/min that guides give for EPS, and is done in 50 s of the 70 s limit; it has not been tried on a real cutter. One grip could steer the block: both arms are not forced.
